decisions.reason: The foldable large container remains a differentiated option with several models and unresolved demand, and its keeping cost is low enough to hold the option.
As a standard, undifferentiated crate with no observed traction after four years, its option value has likely expired, so dropping it frees resources.
The medium-duty rackable pallet is a low-differentiation standard line with no positive signal, and holding it no longer offers sufficient option value.
The spill-retention pallet addresses persistent environmental-compliance needs and still holds option value at low cost.
The load-retainer pallet is differentiated and cheap to keep while demand uncertainty persists.
